› Write a 200 word story about a lighthouse keeper.


• For forty years, Elias lit the lighthouse before sunset, polished its windows, and wrote the weather in a ledger. Ships came and
  went without knowing his name. He preferred it that way, until one November evening when the sea delivered a small red mitten to
  the steps outside his door.

  He hung it beside the stove. The next morning, another mitten appeared, followed by a wooden horse, then a photograph sealed
  inside a jar. It showed a girl standing beside a lighthouse he recognized, though the tower had been demolished long before he
  was born. She was holding his hand.

  Elias searched the old ledgers. Beneath an entry dated eighty years earlier, he found his handwriting: Tonight, keep the light
  burning past dawn. He read the sentence until the letters blurred. Then he filled the lamp, trimmed its wick, and settled into
  his chair to wait for whatever came next.

  At sunrise, a boat emerged from the mist. The girl stood in its bow, bare hands gripping the rail. Elias carried the mittens
  down the steps. He had questions ready, but she was shivering, so he wrapped his coat around her and led her inside. The lamp
  still needed tending.
